issue: Relationship weight is not editable via the graph UI
actual: Clicking (single or double) an edge/relationship label (e.g. "Edge from agile to collab", 50%) only toggles a visual "active"/selected state on the edge (confirmed via aria-current/active attribute and re-snapshot). No dialog, popover, panel, or inline input appears anywhere in the DOM (checked via querySelectorAll('[role=\"dialog\"],[role=\"alertdialog\"],.modal,[data-state=\"open\"]') = empty array both before and after single/double click) that would allow changing the edge weight percentage. No other UI element on the page exposes per-edge weight editing.
evidence: Edge weight labels remain static (80%, 70%, 90%, 60%, 50%) after click/dblclick; only CSS class changes to indicate selection.

issue: Enable/disable toggle inside competency node is non-functional
actual: Clicking the "enabled" switch inside a competency node (e.g. Agile Methodology, role=switch aria-checked=true) does not change aria-checked/data-state. Root cause identified via DOM inspection: every interactive control inside .react-flow__node (switch, level buttons, weight slider) lacks the required React Flow "nodrag" class (checked buttonSample/sliderInfo/switchInfo via browser_evaluate - hasNodrag:false for all 36 inner buttons, both sliders, both switches). Because the whole node div is a React Flow draggable node, React Flow's pointer-drag handling intercepts/swallows the pointerdown before it reaches the nested switch's click handler, so the click has no effect on the underlying state despite Playwright reporting a successful click.
evidence: semantic_snapshot(scope: model.graph) before and after the toggle click showed agile competency unchanged (Intermediate/50%, switch still checked); DOM query confirms 0 of the inner interactive elements carry the nodrag class React Flow requires to exempt them from node drag/click interception.

issue: Competency level selector inside graph node is non-functional
actual: Clicked "set-level-4" control on Code Review competency (data-semtag-id model.graph.item.code-review.set-level-4) intending to raise its level from Intermediate. Playwright reported a successful click with no error, but a re-check via semantic_observe(model.graph.item.code-review.level-value) immediately after showed the level unchanged at "Intermediate". Same root cause as FT-5: the level buttons live inside a React Flow draggable node and lack the "nodrag" class, so pointerdown is captured by the node's drag/click-suppression logic instead of reaching the button's onClick handler.

issue: Weight slider inside graph node does not update value
actual: Focused the Code Review weight slider thumb directly via JS focus() (bypassing any pointer/drag interception - confirmed document.activeElement === thumb, aria-valuenow="60"), then dispatched a genuine ArrowRight keypress via Playwright's real keyboard (page.keyboard.press). A working Radix slider should increment aria-valuenow by its step on ArrowRight even without pointer interaction. After the keypress, aria-valuenow remained "60" and the displayed Weight text remained "60%" - the slider does not respond to keyboard interaction either, indicating the value-change handler itself is not wired up (not merely a pointer/nodrag issue).
evidence: aria-valuenow="60" before and after ArrowRight keypress while thumb held focus; weight-value observable unchanged at 60%.

Selected Training scenario tab (category adjustments: technical +1 level, domain +1 level, 0% weight change) - selecting the tab alone produced a live preview shift in top metrics (Coverage 68%->69%, Avg Level 3.3->3.4). Clicking "Run Simulation" applied the scenario fully: Coverage rose to 81%, Avg Level rose to 4.0, and a new "Model Healthy - All competencies are at or above recommended levels with 81% coverage." alert appeared, consistent with +1 level applied to the 3 technical + 1 domain competencies. Reset button is available to revert. This confirms scenario simulation correctly computes and displays hypothetical impact on model metrics.

actual: Clicked "Apply" on the Product Manager template card while viewing the Software Engineer model. Result: model.title changed to "Product Manager", model.department changed to "Product", metrics updated to Product Manager values (Coverage 78%, Avg Level 3.8, Critical Path 4), and the Template Library correctly re-marked Product Manager as "Current" (Apply now disabled) while Software Engineer lost its "Current" badge. However, the competency graph itself was NOT updated: it still rendered the original Software Engineer competencies verbatim (Programming Languages/System Design/Code Review/Problem Solving/Collaboration/Agile Methodology with unchanged descriptions, levels, and weights, plus the same 5 edges), instead of Product Manager's competencies. The page title, metrics, and graph are now inconsistent with each other.
evidence: Post-apply model.title="Product Manager" / model.department="Product" / metrics.coverage="78%" but model.graph items unchanged: prog-lang/sys-design/code-review/problem-solve/collab/agile with identical names, levels (Advanced/Intermediate), and weights (90%/80%/60%/90%/70%/50%) as the original Software Engineer model.

issue: "Save Current" as template produces no effect
actual: Clicked "Save Current" button in the Template Library panel intending to save the active model as a new reusable template. No naming dialog/prompt appeared (checked DOM for [role=dialog]/[role=alertdialog] = empty), no confirmation toast appeared (the Sonner notifications region <ol> remained empty immediately after click), and the Template Library list was unchanged (still exactly 5 templates: Software Engineer, Product Manager, HR Manager, Data Scientist, Sales Manager - no 6th entry for the newly "saved" template).
evidence: templates.list collection identical before and after click; toast/notification region empty; no dialog opened.

issue: Export and Share actions produce no observable effect
actual: Clicked "Export" button: no dialog/menu opened, no toast/notification fired, no new network request issued (checked browser_network_requests, no non-static request triggered), and no console log/error indicating a download was initiated. evidence: Post-click DOM query for [role=dialog],[role=alertdialog],[role=menu],[data-sonner-toast] returned empty arrays for both buttons; network_requests showed no new requests after either click.

All 6 weight sliders in the competency graph declare aria-valuemin="10" and aria-valuemax="100" (supported range 10%-100%), and every current competency weight value (90%, 80%, 60%, 90%, 70%, 50%) falls within that declared range - confirming the 10-100% weight constraint is correctly defined and consistently respected across the model's data. Note: actual runtime enforcement of the constraint (e.g. rejecting/clamping an out-of-range input) could not be exercised because the weight slider control itself does not respond to any input (see FT-7 FAIL - a separate, broader interactivity defect covering all values, not specific to out-of-range values).

Clicking a competency node (Programming Languages) on the graph adds the "selected" CSS class to the node (react-flow__node ... selected selectable) and produces a distinct visual highlight - selected node box-shadow "rgba(13,162,231,0.3) 0 0 24px -4px" vs. unselected node box-shadow "rgba(19,23,32,0.1) 0 4px 16px -4px" - giving clear visual feedback that the node is selected, without triggering navigation or any unintended side effect.

Zoom in control button correctly increases the graph viewport scale (.react-flow__viewport transform scale 0.7358 -> 0.8829 after one click, translate also recentered), confirming the graph zoom-in interaction works and updates the canvas in real time.

Clicking "toggle interactivity" control removed "draggable", "selectable", and "nopan" classes from all graph nodes (nodeClass changed from "react-flow__node react-flow__node-competency nopan selected selectable draggable" to plain "react-flow__node react-flow__node-competency"), correctly disabling node dragging/selection. Clicking the same control again restored interactivity. This confirms the toggle-interactivity control functions as intended.

The "Critical Path" metric card lists exactly 3 competencies (Programming Languages, Problem Solving, System Design) with count "3". Cross-checking the graph nodes directly, exactly those same 3 nodes carry a "Critical" badge (Programming Languages: true, System Design: true, Problem Solving: true; Code Review/Collaboration/Agile Methodology: false) - the displayed Critical badges are fully consistent with the Critical Path summary metric, confirming accurate content rendering.

Each competency node's 5-segment level indicator bar correctly correlates with its textual Level label: nodes labeled "Advanced" (Programming Languages, Problem Solving) render 4 of 5 level segments filled, while nodes labeled "Intermediate" (System Design, Code Review, Collaboration, Agile Methodology) render 3 of 5 filled - a strictly monotonic, consistent visual encoding of level text across all 6 competencies with no mismatches.

Category badges (technical/behavioral/domain) render with consistent, category-specific text colors across every node: all "technical" badges (Programming Languages, System Design, Code Review) use rgb(13,162,231); both "behavioral" badges (Problem Solving, Collaboration) use rgb(42,157,144); the "domain" badge (Agile Methodology) uses rgb(33,196,93) - confirming accurate and internally consistent content/styling mapping for competency category metadata.
